sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A large rosette succulent native from southern Mexico to Guatemala and widely cultivated. Its stiff leaves are about 1–1.8 m long, with marginal teeth and a terminal spine; the flowering stalk reaches about 5–7 m. The rosette dies after flowering, while offsets can continue the clump.

sections.title: Uses and safety
sections.text: Its leaf fibre, henequen, is used to make rope and twine. The sources cited here document fibre use, not food use.
